A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DST corruption-robustness study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v2 do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original dense-versus-DST experiments on image and video classification, together with frequency, weight-distribution, augmentation and out-of-domain analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and adds clean and corrupted Pascal VOC 2012 segmentation results in Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: The core DST algorithms remain unchanged. Appendix A.9 adds a segmentation-specific adaptation: pruning a pretrained VGG16 backbone before sparse fine-tuning, instead of the randomly initialized sparse topology used for classification.

E1.justification: Appendix A.9 extends evaluation from image/video classification to semantic segmentation on clean and corrupted Pascal VOC 2012, including 19 corruptions at five severities. This introduces a distinct pixel-level prediction task. Existing classification coverage, including the relocated Fashion-MNIST experiment, is retained.

E2.justification: AC/DC comparison rows disappear from v1 Tables 5-8, corresponding to v2 Tables 4-7. AC/DC remains in the TinyImageNet resource-versus-robustness comparison in Figure 9 and its discussion. The other existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new segmentation protocol evaluates FCN-VGG16 at sparsities 0.1 and 0.2 using pixel accuracy and mIoU, with 80 training epochs reported in Table 3. That table also reports 80 UCF101 epochs, conflicting with the 100 epochs stated in both versions' Section 4.3; this reporting change does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: The distinct TinyImageNet-C corruption/severity analysis in v1 Figure 15 is replaced in v2 by a duplicate of the CIFAR100-C plot in Figure 13, despite retaining the TinyImageNet-C caption. The spatial, spectral, Mixup, out-of-domain and Grad-CAM analyses otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs with three fixed seeds for CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and TinyImageNet. Existing uncertainty displays and Fashion-MNIST mean-plus/minus entries are retained. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run reporting are introduced.

E6.justification: The headline classification results remain unchanged. New Table 12 reports corrupted-VOC mIoU of 22.60 for dense training, 22.73 for SET at sparsity 0.2 and 23.09 at 0.1. AC/DC resource entries are removed, and Figure 15 replaces its previous TinyImageNet-C results with the duplicated CIFAR100-C plot.

T1.justification: The distribution-shift assumptions, sparsity definitions and radius-accuracy equations retain their meaning. Section 3.1 compresses the probability-factorization explanation. The added aliasing discussion is conceptual and introduces no new formal result, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the DSCR hypothesis: low-sparsity DST can improve corruption robustness over dense training, with implicit regularization favoring informative features. The segmentation evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation connecting reduced high-frequency dependence with prior work on aliasing during downsampling, and expands the hard-versus-soft sparsity motivation. Appendix A.3.2 explicitly qualifies the reported computational savings as theoretical rather than fully realized on current hardware.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3.1 substantially fills implementation gaps for the existing DeiT, UCF101 and Fashion-MNIST experiments through optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size and topology-update settings. It also supplies the segmentation configuration and codebase/library links. These are mainly new disclosures, although the UCF101 epoch count is inconsistent with the main text.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on frequency aliasing, sparse hardware/software and recent DST developments, including Li, Grabinski, Dey and Wu, plus the VOC reference. These additions contextualize the existing argument without substantially changing its novelty positioning. The JaxPruner publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 expands introductory motivation, streamlines the problem definition, moves the CHT subsection from Section 6.1 to Appendix A.6, and adjusts subsequent appendix organization. It also adds acknowledgements and the ICLR publication header. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 expands the hyperparameter table, adds the segmentation table, removes AC/DC rows and relocates existing displays. Figure captions correct SET labels and explain severity shading; Figure 19 is enlarged. Figure 15 also acquires the duplicated plot. These are localized display and layout changes within the retained presentation.

improvement.justification: The segmentation evidence, fuller implementation documentation and explicit hardware-efficiency qualification improve breadth and transparency. However, v2 replaces the distinct TinyImageNet-C Figure 15 with a duplicated CIFAR100-C plot, introduces conflicting UCF101 epoch counts and removes detailed AC/DC comparisons. With the main conclusions and headline results unchanged, these benefits and losses in reporting reliability leave the net quality direction uncertain.
